material_systems.name: Acrylic Stain-Block Primer for Fiber Cement Siding Repaint
material_systems.description: 100% acrylic exterior stain-blocking primer for previously painted fiber cement siding where existing paint has failed or peeled. Primary RP primer for intact painted areas surrounding bare spots on SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT and SS_EXT_PEELING conditions. Spot prime when localized failure; full prime on SS_EXT_PEELING. Not used on SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (skip prime) or SS_EXT_CHALKING (use chalk-binding instead). Previously painted FC substrate absorbs less than NC bare FC -- higher coverage per gallon. Distinct from NC SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_ACRYLIC which is for bare factory-primed substrate -- this is for existing paint with adhesion concerns.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec EXT Primer
products.notes: Stain-blocking adhesion primer for previously painted FC siding areas. Spot prime scraped/feathered bare areas when localized; full prime when SS_EXT_PEELING or widespread failure. Applied over intact painted areas surrounding bare FC spots (bare FC spots get alkali-resistant primer instead). spray_backroll or brush_roll application.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime feathered areas and surrounding paint; full prime if widespread
prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_PEELING: full surface prime after heavy scrape to sound substrate

material_systems.notes: RP-SPECIFIC primer system. Same product family as SYS_EXT_SFRP_PRIMER_ACRYLIC_RP from SF_SOFFIT_EXT_RP and SYS_EXT_TRRP_PRIMER_ACRYLIC from SF_TRIM_EXT_RP. Adapted for SF-based siding coverage model. No overhead waste factor (vertical application).

material_systems.name: Chalk-Binding Primer for Chalking Exterior Fiber Cement Siding
material_systems.description: Low-viscosity chalk-binding conditioner primer that penetrates and binds loose chalk residue on previously painted fiber cement siding. MANDATORY for SS_EXT_CHALKING regardless of quality tier. Full surface application required -- chalk binding must be uniform. Apply after low-pressure rinse and 24-48 hour dry time. Higher material consumption than standard acrylic primer due to aggressive absorption by chalk residue. Chalking is the MOST COMMON FC siding RP degradation mode -- primary degradation via UV binder breakdown on south/west elevations after 8-12 years.

products.notes: MANDATORY for chalking FC siding. Penetrates and binds loose chalk particles left after low-pressure rinse. Do NOT skip -- topcoat adhesion failure guaranteed without chalk-binding step. Full surface application required. Chalking is the single most common FC siding RP scenario -- many FC repaint jobs are chalking-only with no mechanical failure.

material_systems.notes: RP-SPECIFIC primer system. Same product family as SYS_EXT_SFRP_PRIMER_CHALK_BIND from SF_SOFFIT_EXT_RP. Chalk-binding primer has lower coverage (~250-350 SF/gal on vertical FC siding) due to thicker body required for chalk penetration. Surface texture modifier applies (cedarmill/roughsawn absorb more).

material_systems.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer for Bare Fiber Cement (Reuse NC)
material_systems.description: Alkali-resistant acrylic masonry primer for exposed bare fiber cement areas where paint has failed or peeled, revealing cementitious substrate at pH 13.0. Required on ALL bare FC areas to prevent saponification (alkaline burn) of latex binders. In RP context, applied as spot primer on exposed bare FC areas -- not full surface unless extensive failure exposes large areas. Reuses NC system SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_ALKALI unchanged -- same product, same chemistry, spot application mode in RP.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec Masonry & Stucco Primer
products.notes: MANDATORY on exposed bare fiber cement areas (pH 13.0). Standard acrylic primer is NOT suitable -- causes saponification. Spot prime scraped-to-bare areas in RP. SW Loxon Masonry Primer is the reference product per field experience. Same product as NC -- chemistry is substrate-driven, not condition-driven.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime exposed bare fiber cement areas at failure points
prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_PEELING: spot prime all exposed bare fiber cement; full prime if extensive bare exposure

material_systems.notes: Reuses NC system SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_ALKALI unchanged. Same product, spot application mode in RP. Coverage profile uses COV_FCRP_PRIMER_ALKALI_SPOT (SF-based, fraction of total siding area). Bare FC in RP typically occurs at butt joints, caulk failure points, and areas where paint has peeled back to substrate.

material_systems.name: Bonding Primer for Factory-Finished Fiber Cement Substrate (Reuse NC)
material_systems.description: Bonding primer / adhesion promoter for exposed factory-finished (ColorPlus/ExpertFinish) substrate revealed when RP scraping removes both field paint and underlying factory-primed layer, exposing the original oven-baked factory finish. Secondary/rare primer path in RP context. Reuses NC system SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_BONDING unchanged.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Insl-X Stix Bonding Primer
products.notes: Required when RP scraping exposes original oven-baked factory finish (ColorPlus/ExpertFinish) underneath field paint. Rare in RP -- most FC siding is standard factory-primed, not factory-finished. Light scuff sand exposed factory finish before priming. Spot prime exposed areas only.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_PEELING: spot prime all exposed factory-finished areas

material_systems.notes: Reuses NC system SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_BONDING unchanged. Secondary primer path -- activated only when underlying substrate is ColorPlus/ExpertFinish. Estimator identifies by characteristic multi-coat factory finish color at exposed areas. Coverage profile shared with NC bonding primer.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Finish for Fiber Cement (Reuse NC)
material_systems.description: Standard production 100% acrylic exterior paint for fiber cement siding repaint at QT2/QT3. Hardie-approved products required for warranty compliance. Flat and satin sheen. NOT fine-finish -- standard exterior field coating. Once surface is prepped and primed, finish application is identical to NC except for application method (spray_backroll in RP vs spray-only in NC). QT2: single finish coat. QT3: 2 finish coats per Hardie warranty.

products.notes: Hardie-approved standard exterior acrylic. QT2: single finish coat on properly prepped/primed surface. QT3: 2 finish coats per Hardie warranty. spray_backroll primary (sprayer leads, backroller follows within wet edge). brush_roll fallback for <750 SF, occupied-adjacent, or high wind.

material_systems.notes: Reuses NC system SYS_EXT_FC_FINISH_STANDARD unchanged. Same product -- only application method differs (spray_backroll in RP vs spray-only in NC). Prepped and primed RP surface is equivalent to NC primed surface for finish coat purposes.

material_systems.name: Premium Exterior Finish for Fiber Cement (Reuse NC)
material_systems.description: Premium 100% acrylic exterior paint for QT4 fiber cement siding repaint. Hardie-approved premium products with superior color retention and fade resistance. Light sand between coats (220-grit). 2 finish coats standard. spray_backroll primary. Flat and satin sheen for siding field.

products.notes: James Hardie-approved premium products. Superior color retention, fade resistance. Light sand between coats (220-grit) at QT4. Raking light inspection before second coat. spray_backroll application -- sprayer leads, backroller follows.

material_systems.notes: Reuses NC system SYS_EXT_FC_FINISH_PREMIUM. Flat and satin only for siding field (NC allows semi-gloss at QT4 for accent areas -- RP siding field restricts to flat/satin per sheen resolution). Same product, spray_backroll application.

SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT.notes: Acrylic stain-block primer on previously painted FC siding with localized failures. Spot prime scraped/feathered areas. Higher coverage than NC primer on bare FC (375 vs 275 SF/gal) because RP substrate is partially sealed by existing paint film. Smooth surface baseline.

SS_EXT_PEELING.notes: Acrylic stain-block primer on peeling FC siding -- full surface prime after heavy scrape. More bare exposure = lower coverage than FAILING_PAINT. Applied over intact painted areas; bare FC spots get alkali-resistant primer.

assumptions: Previously painted substrate -- lower absorption than NC bare FC on intact painted areas
Spot prime for SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT covers 15-30% of siding surface (typical localized failure at butt joints and caulk failure points)
Full prime for SS_EXT_PEELING covers 100% of surface after heavy scrape
Surface texture modifier from NC spec transfers unchanged -- physical characteristic
Spray_backroll application: multiply material quantity by 1.25-1.33 for 50-70% transfer efficiency

coverage_rate.notes: Chalk-binding primer on chalking FC siding surface. Full surface application required -- binding must be uniform. Lower coverage (~300 SF/gal) than standard acrylic due to thicker body and aggressive chalk absorption. Heavy chalk on south/west elevations = low end (250 SF/gal). Light chalk = high end (350 SF/gal). Higher than soffit chalk-binding (250 SF/gal) because no overhead waste on vertical siding.

assumptions: Full surface application mandatory -- chalk binding must be uniform
Low-pressure rinse first to remove loose chalk; primer binds remaining residue
Chalk severity drives coverage range: heavy chalk = low end, light chalk = high end
Vertical application -- no overhead waste factor (unlike soffit)
Spray_backroll application: multiply material quantity by 1.25-1.33 for transfer efficiency

SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT.notes: Alkali-resistant primer on exposed bare fiber cement areas. Spot prime at failure points. Bare FC is highly porous -- lowest coverage primer in this spec. Same rate as NC COV_FCSD_PRIMER_ALKALI.

SS_EXT_PEELING.notes: Alkali-resistant primer on extensively exposed bare FC. More bare substrate = greater absorption. Heavy peeling on butt joints and caulk failure areas with large bare exposure.

assumptions: Spot priming exposed bare fiber cement areas only -- not full surface unless extensive failure
Typical bare FC exposure in RP: 10-30% of siding surface at butt joints, caulk failure points, board end wicking
Bare fiber cement is highly porous -- lowest coverage of any primer
Surface texture modifiers slightly lower than NC (1.15/1.25 vs 1.20/1.30) because bare FC at failure points tends to be at edges where texture is less pronounced
Coverage rates match NC COV_FCSD_PRIMER_ALKALI baseline

coverage_rate.notes: Bonding primer on exposed factory-finished (ColorPlus) FC substrate. Factory-finished surface is smooth and non-porous -- good coverage. Spot prime at exposed areas only. Same rate as NC COV_FCSD_PRIMER for bonding system. Rare RP scenario.

assumptions: Spot priming exposed factory-finished areas only
Factory-finished surface is non-porous -- consistent coverage
Typical exposure in RP: 5-15% of siding surface (rare scenario)
Coverage matches NC bonding primer rate

lap.notes: Finish coat on prepped/primed FC lap siding via spray_backroll. Slightly lower than NC spray-only (350 SF/gal) because backroll redistributes product -- net ~5-10% more material consumption vs spray-only. Long horizontal runs.

panel.notes: Finish coat on large flat FC panels via spray_backroll. Slightly better coverage than lap due to fewer edges and transitions. Backroll redistribution effect is smaller on flat panels.

shingle.notes: Finish coat on FC shingle siding via spray_backroll. Many edges, overlapping profiles, complex geometry. Highest material consumption per SF. Backroll is especially important on shingle for working product into lapped edges.

SYS_EXT_FC_FINISH_STANDARD.notes: Standard acrylic -- baseline coverage rates above

SYS_EXT_FC_FINISH_PREMIUM.notes: Premium acrylic has higher solids -- slightly lower coverage per gallon (~7% reduction). Multiply sf_per_gallon by 0.93.

assumptions: Coverage is per NET siding area from PaintScope (PS_EXT_SURFACE_SF.SIDING_FIELD)
Prepped and primed RP surface -- coverage equivalent to NC after prime, adjusted for spray_backroll vs spray-only
Two-coat system at QT3/QT4. QT2 single coat on primed surface.
Spray_backroll application: multiply material quantity by 1.25-1.33 for transfer efficiency
Backroll redistribution adds ~5-10% material consumption vs NC spray-only -- baked into profile rates above
Surface texture modifier from NC spec transfers unchanged

consumables.name: RP Assessment Kit (adhesion + chalk + moisture + mildew test)
consumables.specification: Cross-hatch cutter, pressure-sensitive tape (ASTM D3359), white cloth for chalk rub test, moisture meter, mildew swab test, biocide assessment supplies
consumables.notes: RP-specific assessment supplies. One kit per project. Includes ASTM D3359 cross-hatch adhesion test (critical on chalking surfaces where adhesion may appear sound), white cloth for chalk rub test, moisture meter for siding joints and areas with visible water damage, mildew/algae severity assessment. Shared across exterior RP specs.

consumables.name: Mildewcide / Biocide Solution
consumables.specification: Mildewcide / biocide concentrate (sodium hypochlorite solution or commercial mildew remover), mix per manufacturer directions
consumables.notes: Apply during wash or as separate pre-wash treatment for mildew/algae on FC siding. Common on north-facing and shaded elevations in humid climates. Kill mildew BEFORE painting -- painting over mildew = guaranteed adhesion failure. Allow 10-15 min dwell time, rinse with low-pressure water. 1 QT concentrate per ~100 SF of treated surface at typical dilution. Shared across exterior RP specs.

consumables.name: Liquid Sander / Deglosser
consumables.specification: Liquid sander/deglosser, Krud Kutter Gloss-Off or equivalent
consumables.notes: RP-specific: chemical degloss for existing paint on SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT FC siding. Dulls existing sheen to promote adhesion without full mechanical sanding. One quart covers ~200 SF of siding surface. Shared across RP specs.

consumables.name: Carbide Scraper (Exterior Paint Scraping)
consumables.specification: Carbide scraper with replaceable blades, rigid and flexible profiles
consumables.notes: Exterior-specific tool for scraping failing/peeling paint on FC siding. Carbide blades last longer than steel on exterior paint buildup. FC cementitious surface dulls blades faster than wood. One scraper covers ~500 SF of siding scraping before blade replacement. Shared across exterior RP specs.

consumables.name: Efflorescence Neutralizer (Dilute Acetic Acid)
consumables.specification: Dilute acetic acid (vinegar solution) or commercial efflorescence remover
consumables.notes: FC-SPECIFIC: For neutralizing heavy efflorescence deposits (white crystalline salt deposits) on fiber cement siding. Efflorescence is a cementitious substrate failure mode not found on wood siding. Apply, 10-15 min dwell, rinse. If efflorescence is active (recurring after cleaning), moisture source must be addressed before painting. 1 QT per ~50 SF of heavy efflorescence treatment.

consumables.name: Exterior Polyurethane Paintable Caulk
consumables.specification: Polyurethane or siliconized acrylic exterior caulk, paintable, 10.3 oz cartridge
consumables.notes: RP-SPECIFIC: Higher-performance caulk for RP joint replacement on FC siding. Polyurethane or siliconized acrylic -- better adhesion and flexibility than standard caulk for re-caulking applications. MAJOR consumable for FC siding RP -- every butt joint, siding-to-trim junction, window/door perimeter, foundation transition. Typical residential FC siding: 8-15 tubes per project (200-500 LF total joints). Assess condition per 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol. NEVER silicone -- not paintable. 2-4 hr cure before overcoating.

consumables.name: 80-120 Grit Sandpaper for Feather-Edge Sanding
consumables.notes: 80-120 grit for feather-edge sanding after scraping on failing/peeling FC siding. Creates smooth transition from scraped bare areas to intact paint. Hand blocks for detail areas, orbital sander for field.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-180 Grit
consumables.notes: General prep sanding on FC siding and degloss scuffing on sound paint surfaces. Also used for adhesion prep on previously painted surfaces before priming. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 Grit
consumables.notes: For intercoat sanding at QT4 between finish coats. Light scuff for adhesion and defect leveling. Also used for degloss scuffing on factory-finished (ColorPlus) exposed substrate before bonding primer. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Tack Cloth
consumables.notes: Dust removal after sanding before prime or finish coat. Required after all sanding operations. Vertical siding: 150 SF per cloth (better than overhead 100 SF). Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: 18-inch Roller Cover for Backroll (3/8 or 1/2 nap)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 400 SF rolled (primer or finish per coat)
consumables.notes: RP-SPECIFIC: 18-inch roller cover for spray_backroll operation. Follows sprayed product into surface for adhesion on weathered existing paint film. 3/8 nap for smooth FC siding, 1/2 nap for cedarmill/roughsawn texture profiles. NC does not backroll on FC -- this consumable is RP-only. 2-person operation: sprayer leads, backroller follows within wet edge. Higher consumption rate on textured profiles.

consumables.name: Angled Sash Brush 2.5 inch
consumables.notes: Primary brush for detail work -- cut-in at siding-to-trim junctions, spot prime edges, corner detail, under-lap touch-up. Per convention: 1 brush per material type. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Airless Spray Tip 517 (lap/panel siding)
consumables.notes: 515 or 517 fan pattern for lap and panel siding. Sound or chalking surface uses same tips as NC. Failing/peeling with significant bare areas may benefit from 519 for increased deposition. Reused from NC spec. Cementitious substrate causes slightly faster tip wear than wood.

consumables.name: Airless Spray Tip 413 (shingle profile)
consumables.notes: Smaller fan pattern for shingle profiles -- complex geometry requires tighter spray pattern. Higher tip wear from constant angle changes. Reused from NC spec.

consumables.name: 60-mesh Spray Filter (black) for Latex
consumables.notes: Standard 60-mesh (black) filter for latex exterior coatings through airless equipment. Change when flow rate drops. Reused from NC spec.

consumables.name: Painter's Tape (exterior grade UV-resistant 14-day)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum for multi-day exterior projects. Used for trim edge masking (MANDATORY in RP -- trim is almost always already finished), light fixture masking, siding edge masking. RP requires MORE masking than NC because all adjacent surfaces are finished. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Masking Film/Paper for Adjacent Trim Protection
consumables.notes: Masking film or paper for protecting finished trim from siding spray overspray and backroll spatter. In RP, adjacent trim (corner boards, frieze, casings) is almost always already painted -- protection is MANDATORY. Tape + 12-inch film along trim-siding junctions. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Plastic Sheeting / Landscape Tarps
consumables.notes: 4 mil minimum for landscape, hardscape, and HVAC unit protection. UV-resistant for multi-day exterior projects. RP requires wider coverage than NC -- scraping debris and rinse water runoff in addition to overspray. Reused from NC spec.

consumables.name: Canvas Drop Cloths
consumables.notes: Heavy canvas drop cloths for hardscape walkway and patio protection. Non-slip surface for crew traffic. RP also catches scraping debris. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: 6-Mil Poly Sheeting (RRP Containment)
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. 6-mil poly for ground containment extending 10 ft from structure per EPA RRP Rule. Per-elevation quantity. Very rare for FC siding (introduced ~1987) but required for EPA compliance when BUILDING is pre-1978. Shared across all exterior RP specs.

ext_landscape_perimeter.description: House perimeter where landscape is adjacent -- measured in LF along foundation/siding line
ext_landscape_perimeter.notes: LF-based (per UC-001 from NC). RP landscape protection covers scraping debris and rinse water runoff in addition to NC overspray coverage. Brush/roll GOOD condition: drop cloth at base. Brush/roll FAIR/POOR (scraping): full cover. Spray_backroll: full tarp width over plantings. RRP: 6-mil poly per EPA containment rule.

ext_hardscape_walk.notes: Canvas drop cloths for non-slip crew traffic. Plastic sheeting for spray overspray. RP also catches scraping debris.

ext_hardscape_patio.notes: Protection level driven by proximity and application method.

ext_light_fixture.description: Exterior light fixtures on or adjacent to siding
ext_light_fixture.notes: Bag or tape over fixture. Remove fixture cover plate if accessible. Same as NC.

ext_hvac_unit.description: HVAC condenser units adjacent to siding
ext_hvac_unit.notes: Full tarp cover during spray_backroll operations. Do not block intake/exhaust if unit is running.

ext_vehicle_driveway.description: Vehicle and driveway overspray protection -- RP occupied home context
ext_vehicle_driveway.notes: RP-SPECIFIC: Occupied home context -- vehicles and driveway are adjacent during spray operations. Spray overspray on vehicles is a liability. Not needed for brush_roll (no overspray). Shared with other exterior RP specs.

ext_ground_cover.description: General ground protection below siding work zone for scraping debris
ext_ground_cover.notes: RP-SPECIFIC: Ground protection for scraping debris, rinse water runoff, and paint drips during prep. Active for SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT and SS_EXT_PEELING conditions where scraping generates debris. Wider coverage than landscape-only zone because scraping sends debris outward.

ext_rrp_containment.description: EPA RRP Rule containment for pre-1978 buildings
ext_rrp_containment.notes: RP-SPECIFIC: 6-mil poly extending 10 ft from structure per EPA RRP Rule. Required when pre_1978 + lead. Per-elevation setup/teardown. Very rare for FC siding but required for compliance when BUILDING is pre-1978. Shared across all exterior RP specs.

compatibility_rules.description: Sound paint with verified adhesion -- skip prime entirely
compatibility_rules.notes: Existing paint is sound and adhesion verified via ASTM D3359. No primer needed. Degloss/scuff existing surface and proceed to finish coats. Common FC siding RP scenario for well-maintained homes.

MANDATORY. Most common FC siding RP scenario. Topcoat adhesion failure guaranteed without chalk-binding step. Full surface application required. Chalking is the primary degradation mode for FC siding -- UV binder breakdown, especially on south/west elevations after 8-12 years.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing/peeling paint -- acrylic stain-block RP primer on painted areas + alkali-resistant on exposed bare FC
compatibility_rules.notes: Dual primer path: alkali-resistant primer (SW Loxon) on ALL exposed bare FC areas (pH 13.0 -- saponification risk), bonding primer on exposed ColorPlus substrate (rare), and acrylic stain-block on remaining painted areas needing adhesion primer. Spot prime for localized SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT; full prime for SS_EXT_PEELING.

compatibility_rules.description: No power washing on fiber cement -- low-pressure rinse only
compatibility_rules.notes: CRITICAL: High-pressure power washing PROHIBITED on fiber cement in ALL contexts including RP. Strips existing paint films, damages embossed texture (cedarmill, roughsawn), forces water behind wall assembly through butt joints and J-channels. Low-pressure rinse only: 400-600 PSI max with wide fan tip (40-60 degree). CRITICAL departure from wood siding RP (1000-1500 PSI). Transfers from NC COMPAT-005.

compatibility_rules.description: Hardie-approved finish products for warranty compliance
compatibility_rules.notes: James Hardie warranty requires approved paint products. SW Duration, SW Emerald, BM Aura, BM Regal Select are approved. Verify PDS compatibility for any substitution. Transfers from NC COMPAT-004.

compatibility_rules.description: Flat and satin sheen only for siding field
compatibility_rules.notes: Siding field is flat or satin only. Semi-gloss and gloss reserved for trim and fine-finish surfaces. Same restriction as NC.

compatibility_rules.description: Mildew/algae present -- biocide treatment mandatory before any coating

then.sequence: biocide treatment -> 10-15 min dwell -> low-pressure rinse -> 24-48 hr dry -> prime/paint

compatibility_rules.notes: MANDATORY. Painting over mildew causes guaranteed adhesion failure as organisms continue growing beneath paint film. Common on north-facing and shaded elevations in humid climates. FC surface resists mold penetration but surface growth is common.

compatibility_rules.description: Efflorescence -- resolve moisture source before painting if active/recurring

then.action: STOP -- resolve moisture source before painting
then.treatment_if_inactive: dry brush deposits, neutralize with CON_FCRP_EFFLORESCENCE_NEUTRALIZER, alkali-resistant primer on affected area

compatibility_rules.notes: FC-SPECIFIC: Efflorescence (white crystalline salt deposits) indicates moisture migrating through cementitious matrix. Surface efflorescence: clean + neutralize + alkali-resistant primer. Active/recurring: STOP painting until moisture source resolved. Paint will fail if moisture pathway is not fixed. FM-003.

compatibility_rules.description: Caulk application sequence -- caulk AFTER prime coat
compatibility_rules.notes: Caulk adheres better to primed surfaces. For FC siding RP, this means: assess caulk during assessment phase, remove failed caulk during prep, prime, THEN re-caulk, then finish. Critical for major joint volume on FC siding.

compatibility_rules.description: Do NOT caulk field butt joints on lap siding -- moisture trap risk
compatibility_rules.notes: NC spec prohibits caulking field butt joints on lap siding -- creates moisture trap behind joint. RP assesses existing butt joint caulk (prior painters may have caulked them) and removes FAILED caulk at active water intrusion points, but does NOT apply NEW caulk to butt joints. Re-caulk only siding-to-trim joints, window/door perimeter, and foundation transitions.

risk_notes.topic: Chalking-induced topcoat delamination -- most common FC siding RP failure
risk_notes.risk: Applying topcoat over chalking FC surface without chalk-binding primer. Chalk layer prevents bonding -- new paint peels within 1-3 years. Most common RP failure mode for fiber cement. Many FC repaint jobs are chalking-only with no mechanical failure, making it easy to skip chalk-binding step.
risk_notes.mitigation: Chalk rub test on EVERY elevation after rinse. Chalk-binding primer (SYS_EXT_FCRP_PRIMER_CHALK_BIND) MANDATORY when chalk is present. Full surface application. No exceptions.

risk_notes.topic: Alkaline burn / saponification at bare FC areas
risk_notes.risk: Applying standard latex primer directly to bare fiber cement (pH 13.0) exposed by scraping. Alkaline environment destroys latex binders -- paint softens, blisters, detaches.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use alkali-resistant primer (SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_ALKALI / SW Loxon Masonry Primer) on ALL exposed bare FC areas. Never apply standard acrylic latex directly to bare fiber cement. Chemistry is substrate-driven -- same risk as NC.

risk_notes.topic: Caulk joint failure causing paint failure at board junctions
risk_notes.risk: Failed caulk at siding-to-trim, butt joints, or window/door perimeter allows water behind siding. Moisture-driven paint failure radiates from failed joint outward. FC siding has significantly more caulked joints than wood siding.
risk_notes.mitigation: 'Think Like a Water Drop' caulk assessment at every joint. Replace all failed caulk before painting. Use flexible paintable caulk (CON_FCRP_CAULK_EXT_POLY). Do NOT caulk field butt joints on lap siding.

risk_notes.risk: Painting over active efflorescence without resolving moisture source. Water continues migrating through cementitious matrix, depositing salts that physically push new paint film off. FC-specific failure mode.
risk_notes.mitigation: Assess efflorescence for recurrence -- clean, wait 48 hr, check for new deposits. If recurring, STOP and resolve moisture source. Neutralize inactive efflorescence + alkali-resistant primer before topcoat.

risk_notes.risk: Airless spray overspray drifts 10-15 ft. RP uses spray_backroll (spray component generates overspray). Can damage plantings, stain concrete, coat vehicles. Occupied home context increases liability.
risk_notes.mitigation: Full landscape/hardscape/vehicle protection for spray_backroll. Wind monitoring -- stop spray if wind exceeds 10 mph. Wider protection zone in RP than NC due to scraping debris and occupied home.

risk_notes.topic: Power washing damage on fiber cement
risk_notes.risk: High-pressure power washing strips existing paint, damages embossed texture, forces water behind wall assembly. Even moderate pressure (1000-1500 PSI) is too high for FC.
risk_notes.mitigation: Low-pressure rinse ONLY: 400-600 PSI max with wide fan tip. This is a CRITICAL departure from wood siding RP (1000-1500 PSI). Garden hose + soft brush for stubborn areas.

risk_notes.topic: RRP lead dust from pre-1978 building siding
risk_notes.risk: FC siding was introduced in ~1987, so most is post-1978. However, siding may have been replaced on a pre-1978 structure where lead is present in other components or prior coating. Scraping generates debris.
risk_notes.mitigation: RRP containment when building is pre-1978 + lead-positive. 6-mil poly 10 ft from structure. Wet scraping methods. Per-elevation setup. Very rare for FC but required for compliance.

material_quantity_notes.spray_transfer_efficiency: Airless spray on FC siding (spray_backroll): 50-70% transfer efficiency. Multiply theoretical coverage by 1.25-1.50 to account for overspray, misting, and pattern overlap. Backroll does not add material -- it redistributes what was sprayed.
material_quantity_notes.backroll_material_impact: Backroll operation adds ~5-10% material consumption vs NC spray-only. Not because backroll uses more product, but because slightly heavier spray pass is needed to maintain wet edge for backroller following sprayer. Baked into RP coverage profiles.
material_quantity_notes.surface_texture_factor: Cedarmill texture: multiply material by 1.20x. Roughsawn texture: multiply by 1.30x. Applied on top of profile coverage rate. Same as NC -- physical characteristic unchanged between NC and RP.
material_quantity_notes.siding_profile_factor: Lap (baseline). Panel: slightly better coverage (fewer edges). Shingle: 25-35% more material due to complex geometry and edge coverage. Same as NC.
material_quantity_notes.coat_system_rp: RP coat system varies by condition: GOOD = finish only (no prime). FAIR/POOR = state-driven prime + finish coats. QT2: 1 finish coat. QT3/QT4: 2 finish coats per Hardie warranty.
material_quantity_notes.spot_prime_coverage: Spot prime area estimate: SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT = 15-30% of siding surface (localized at butt joints and caulk failure points). SS_EXT_PEELING = 40-60%+ (often moisture-driven from behind). Calculate alkali-resistant primer from bare FC area, not total siding SF.
material_quantity_notes.caulk_quantity: Major consumable for FC siding RP. Typical residential: 200-500 LF of joints total. 1 TUBE per 20-25 LF. Typical project: 8-15 tubes. Condition drives replacement percentage: GOOD = near-zero, FAIR = moderate, POOR = extensive.

assumptions.value: 325-375 SF/gal for acrylic RP primer on previously painted FC siding
assumptions.source: NC COV_FCSD_PRIMER adjusted: previously painted substrate absorbs less, no overhead waste (vertical)
assumptions.note: Previously painted substrate (intact areas) absorbs less primer than bare FC. Vertical application -- no overhead waste factor unlike soffit.

assumptions.value: 250-350 SF/gal for chalk-binding primer on chalking FC siding
assumptions.source: SF_SOFFIT_EXT_RP COV_SFRP_PRIMER_CHALK_BIND (250 SF/gal overhead) adjusted up for vertical -- no overhead waste
assumptions.note: Chalk-binding primer is thicker-bodied with lower coverage than standard primer. Vertical siding allows higher coverage per gallon than overhead soffit. South/west elevations have heavier chalk = lower coverage.

assumptions.value: 250-375 SF/gal depending on profile, adjusted from NC spray-only
assumptions.source: NC COV_FCSD_FINISH adjusted down ~5-10% for spray_backroll vs spray-only application
assumptions.note: Backroll redistributes sprayed product into surface irregularities. Requires slightly heavier spray pass to maintain wet edge. Net material consumption ~5-10% higher than NC spray-only.

assumptions.value: 200-500 LF of caulk joints per typical residential FC siding project
assumptions.source: Research RF-006 (caulk assessment is MAJOR scope), Exterior_Caulking_Sealants_Doctrine
assumptions.note: FC siding has significantly more caulked joints than wood siding. No doctrine specifies typical LF per project. Flag for field calibration. Major labor and material line item.

assumptions.value: 1 QT per 50 SF of heavy efflorescence treatment
assumptions.source: FC-specific -- no direct comparable in other exterior RP specs (cementitious substrate only)
assumptions.note: Efflorescence neutralizer coverage rate is estimated. Heavy deposits require more product. Flag for field calibration.

uncertainty_flags.description: The 15-30% spot prime area estimate for SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT is based on typical FC failure patterns (butt joints, caulk failure points, board end wicking). Actual area varies significantly by project. SS_EXT_PEELING may have 40-60%+ bare exposure.
uncertainty_flags.action: Flag for field calibration. Track actual scraped/exposed area as percentage of total siding SF on RP projects.

uncertainty_flags.description: The ~5-10% material premium for spray_backroll vs NC spray-only is estimated. Actual premium depends on backroll operator technique, wet edge management, and surface condition.
uncertainty_flags.action: Track actual material consumption on spray_backroll FC siding RP projects vs NC spray-only for calibration.

uncertainty_flags.description: Caulk joint replacement percentage by condition is estimated: GOOD = near-zero, FAIR = 30-50%, POOR = 60-90%. Actual varies by building age, climate, and caulk product quality.
uncertainty_flags.action: Track actual caulk replacement LF as percentage of total joint LF on FC siding RP projects.

uncertainty_flags.description: Efflorescence neutralizer coverage (1 QT per 50 SF) is estimated for heavy deposits. Light deposits may need less. FC-specific -- no comparable data from other specs.
uncertainty_flags.action: Track actual neutralizer consumption on FC siding with efflorescence. Document efflorescence severity categories.

uncertainty_flags.description: Chalk-binding primer coverage on cedarmill/roughsawn textured FC is estimated using same texture modifier as standard primer (1.20x/1.30x). Actual chalk penetration into textured valleys may differ.
uncertainty_flags.action: Track chalk-binding primer consumption separately for smooth vs textured FC siding profiles.
